thread:
customer-jc: Hey team — hitting a customer outage. Streaming responses over SSE get cut off at the very end (last ~5-15 chars missing) when the client experiences an auth token rotation. Client then reconnects and sometimes receives duplicate final tokens. Customer says this started after they switched to short-lived tokens. Attaching minimal client log excerpt below.

customer-jc: client logs:
  - recv: '...the final sentenc'
  - got 401 mid-stream: 'unauthorized'
  - reconnect -> resume with Last-Event-ID -> got: 'e'
  - server also logged a +1 token billing event for the resumed chunk

support-alex: thanks @customer-jc — can you paste the full request headers (sans PII) and the Last-Event-ID header used for resume? Also which model/route and region?

customer-jc: sure. headers:
  Authorization: Bearer <rotating-token> (rotates every 30s)
  Accept: text/event-stream
  Last-Event-ID: 01c9f2a7
  x-route: /v1/stream/generate
  model: gpt-large-v1
  region: us-west-2

eng-irma: OK, this smells like a race between auth expiring mid-stream and the resume path not replaying the exact suffix of the token stream. Two hypotheses:
  1) Server closes connection on 401 and doesn't emit a terminal SSE event before aborting write buffers, so client sees truncated last event.
  2) Resume path replays the remaining tokens but uses a different event boundary, producing a tiny overlap/duplication and billing counts recorded twice.

eng-irma: Can we get a trace id from their request? support-alex, any request_id in your logs?

support-alex: I pulled the request id: req_0b9a4e2c. Also saw `stream_conn_close` with reason=auth.expired at 2026-11-03T16:02:12.344Z in our logs. No terminal `event: end` was emitted, looks like the stream was aborted.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary v2.14.8 -> redeployed to us-west-2 at 2026-11-03T15:58:03 UTC. No errors reported on deploy.

eng-oncall-maya: Repro attempt plan: simulate short-lived token rotation mid-stream and capture pcap + server traces. Steps:
  1) Start a streaming request with `curl --no-buffer` and a token that expires in 8s.
  2) After 6s, have a proxy return 401 for the same connection to simulate the client noticing token invalidation.
  3) Client reconnects with `Last-Event-ID` header set to last event id.
  4) Collect pcap (tcpdump -i any -w auth-rotate.pcap) and server trace (TRACE=stream:debug).

eng-irma: Good. Add `strace`/`ss` on server to see if write() returned EPIPE or if the runtime aborted before flushing. Also check the SSE framing: are we emitting `data:` lines with trailing double newline and then `event: done`?

customer-jc: I can run a repro against a staging endpoint if you provide the exact curl snippet and env to set.

eng-oncall-maya: use this minimal repro (on customer's machine):

  TOKEN_SHORT=xxxx_short_lived
  curl -v -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN_SHORT" -H "X-Request-Id: req-0b9a4e2c-cust" "https://api.staging.redwood.ai/v1/stream/generate?model=gpt-large-v1" --no-buffer

  Then after 6s, hit the connection with a proxy rule to return 401 for new packets: e.g., `iptables -A OUTPUT -p tcp --dport 443 -m time --tmin 6 --tmax 6 -j REJECT` or use mitmproxy to modify server response.

eng-irma: For server-side capture: run `tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/auth-rotate.pcap host <customer-ip> and port 443` and collect `redwood-runtime.log` with `TRACE=streaming:debug,auth:debug` enabled. Also collect `metrics` snapshot: `curl http://localhost:9100/metrics | egrep "stream_conn|resume_success|billing_tokens"`.

billing-sam: On the billing side, I see an anomaly: one request_id had token_count incremented twice within a 500ms window. Suggest logging `billing.candidate_resume_id` and `billing.duplicate_detect` for resumed streams so we can tie duplicate charges to resume logic.

eng-irma: While we gather traces, quick mitigation ideas:
  - Ensure server emits a final SSE `event: aborted\ndata: auth_expired\n\n` before force-closing connections on auth failure (gives clients a clean termination).
  - Implement idempotent resume semantics: server should dedupe token output for resume attempts using a resume offset or token sequence number in state.
  - Instrument resume path with `resume_seq_start` and `resume_seq_end` so billing can discount overlapped tokens.

support-alex: Customer ran the repro and attached auth-rotate.pcap (uploaded to S3 link). I pulled relevant server logs:

  [2026-11-03T16:02:12.344Z] req=0b9a4e2c conn=conn-77 write_chunk=0 len=1024 err=0
  [2026-11-03T16:02:12.345Z] req=0b9a4e2c conn=conn-77 auth=expired -> closing connection (no graceful finish)
  [2026-11-03T16:02:12.348Z] conn=conn-77 socket: write returned EPIPE
  [2026-11-03T16:02:12.350Z] resume: candidate id=01c9f2a7 tokens_left=8
  [2026-11-03T16:02:12.356Z] resume: success req=0b9a4e2c-resumed tokens_sent=8 billing.tokens=+8

eng-irma: That log chain supports hypothesis 1 & 2. The runtime aborted without a final `event: done` framing. The resumed path duplicated tokens because resume didn't consult an atomic write offset.

eng-oncall-maya: Short-term patch: when auth expiry detected, change code path to first attempt to send a small SSE message `event: auth_expired\ndata: {"code":"auth.expired"}\n\n` and flush. If flush fails, mark stream state as "aborted_no_emit" and set resume base offset to last confirmed sent token rather than last in-memory buffer.

engineering note (eng-irma): adding to backlog: `INFRA-1138 - make resume idempotent by tracking token sequence numbers` and `INFRA-1139 - emit terminal SSE events on auth/timeout`. Prioritize as P1 for Dedicated/hosted customers with short token lifetimes.

support-alex: Customer accepted workaround: increase token TTL > 30s OR implement short polling instead of long-lived SSE until we ship patch. Customer prefers patch.

billing-sam: I'll open a billing investigation ticket to reconcile the duplicate token increments and consider issuing credits where duplicates are verified. Ticket: BILL-4782.

eng-irma: Followups:
  - eng to ship small runtime change that attempts graceful SSE final event on auth expiry (PR today).
  - add metrics and logging for resume dedupe (rollout in next canary).
  - support to coordinate with customer for repro verification in staging.

support-alex: leaving thread for now. If anyone needs more traces, ping me and I'll request the pcap and staging access from the customer. :thumbsup:

customer-jc: thanks all — appreciate the quick triage. Will stand by for patch and can rerun repro when requested. :pray:
